issue: `judge()`'s default implementation passes transcript-derived slice text as a literal CLI argument (`subprocess.run(["claude", "--print", "--model", tier, prompt], ...)`) rather than via a temp file with `-f`, departing from this codebase's own documented dispatch convention (`dispatch-contract.md`: "IMPORTANT: Always use `-f` with a temp file for prompts to avoid shell escaping issues"), which the PRD points at ("the way the `use-sonnet` skill documents"). Not a shell-injection risk here (list-form `subprocess.run`, no `shell=True`), but a long slice can hit OS `ARG_MAX` and crash unguarded.
reason: Real but deliberately deferred to PRD 00008. The inline-argument shape is what this PRD's design doc signed verbatim (Interfaces & contracts, `judge`), and `judge`'s call shape is the one cross-PRD contract this design names: PRD 00008's distiller imports this exact function. Changing its subprocess I/O is a 00008-design decision, not a 00007 rework item. Blake is right that there is no injection risk (list-form argv, no shell=True); the residual is an ARG_MAX ceiling (~1 MB on macOS) against a single assistant text block, which is far below it in practice. Revisit when 00008 designs its strong-tier calls.

Recorded so the divergence stays visible in the PRD's completion record rather than being silently absorbed.

issue: `corpus.py`'s declared export `assert_contract(version)` does not match its actual signature `assert_contract(version: str, parser_module: ModuleType, minimum: str = _MIN_VERSION)` — a second positional argument is required. The fuller Behavior prose ("the check also asserts the imported parser exposes what this skill calls") justifies the extra parameter, but the terse Module Exports line in the PRD promises a one-argument function; a caller going only by that line's contract would hit `TypeError: missing 1 required positional argument`.
reason: The PRD's own Behavior prose for this feature requires the extra parameter ("The check also asserts the imported parser exposes what this skill calls, so a rename in the other repo surfaces as a named failure rather than a wrong result"), and the design doc signed `assert_contract(version, parser_module, minimum=_MIN_VERSION)` verbatim. The terse Module Exports line is a summary of the same feature, not a competing contract. Giving parser_module a default would let the function silently re-resolve the parser, which is exactly the double-resolution defect cycle 1 fixed in task 12.

issue: `_write_report` names files with second-resolution UTC timestamps (`%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ`) and calls `write_text` unconditionally with no existence check — two runs inside the same second would silently overwrite each other's report in `dev/local/audit-results/`. Not specified either way by the PRD, low likelihood given the tool's on-demand solo-maintainer usage, but worth naming under "no unguarded file operations."
reason: Speculative - error handling for a state that cannot occur. distil-memory is an on-demand tool whose runs take seconds to minutes (the recorded real run read 122 transcripts), so two completed runs landing inside the same UTC second is not reachable. Blake himself rates the likelihood low. Adding a uniquifier or an existence check would be defensive code for an impossible state.
